title: Manage content infrastructure
goal: The places the venture keeps content are set up as the storage rules say, the day-to-day keeping of them is someone's named work, and each audit's findings are tracked until they are resolved.

steps.do: Check that each kind of content actually sits where the storage rule says, list every piece that does not, and open a handoff to move it, leaving any tool or account change to the IT function.
Write the recurring keeping work as a process record with one owner, filing new pieces, fixing broken links and retiring pieces past their date, with how often it runs.

Check the live content against the rules that bind it, the approval it needed, the claims it makes with their sources, and the retention period it sits under, and list each breach with the rule it breaks.

Write when content is audited and what each audit covers, the public pages every quarter and the private records once a year, and put the schedule on the process record rather than leaving it to memory.

consider.why: An audit nobody has scheduled happens only after something has already gone out wrong.
consider.when: The venture has public content or content a contract or regulation binds.

steps.do: Run the audit the schedule names on the sample it names, record a pass or a fail per piece against each rule, and keep the sample and the date so the next audit can be compared with this one.
Open one handoff per breach with its owner and due date, report the ones still open past their date, and close a breach only when the piece itself has changed.
Raise to the founder any breach that touches a public claim or a contract term, and to the strategy lead which breaches to fix first.

done_criteria.check: Does every breach name the rule it breaks and stay open until the piece of content itself has changed?
